title: First-Line Supervisors of Retail Sales Workers

tasks.short: Greet customers, answer questions, help with purchases and resolve complaints.

steps.what: Greet the customer and establish what help they need.
Check stock, transaction details and relevant service policy.
Explain options, demonstrate goods and help the customer choose.
For complaints, hear the customer's account and inspect the disputed goods.
Approve and explain a remedy within delegated limits, or escalate.
Record the complaint outcome and send unresolved cases to customer service.

tasks.design: A lookup panel joins stock in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, purchase records in the point-of-sale system {OTHER}, and approved policies in the {DOCS}. A short form in the {HELPDESK} captures the outcome once and routes follow-up automatically; the supervisor approves remedies and handles the conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock, purchases and policies sit in separate screens. Shared mailboxes often carry the unresolved complaint handoff.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard connectors and small deterministic lookup tools can bring verified facts together. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort without requiring automated customer conversations.
tasks.still_hard: Reading distress, inspecting goods and choosing a fair exception remain human work. Receipt access and inconsistent product identifiers can make integration expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, recognise an unstated need and explain a disappointing decision with care.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time searching and forwarding cases, leaving some capacity for booked product help. Remedy authority stays within existing delegated limits.

reach.task: Resolve routine product and return questions.
reach.learn: Learn product identifiers, policy exceptions and effective customer handovers.

evidence.claim: Deterministic lookup and configured complaint routing can reduce searching and duplicate entry; benefits are unmeasured here.
GDPR applies to identifiable customer records; access and retention must follow the service purpose.

assumptions: The store has digital stock and purchase records.
Time shares represent a mixed workload; complaint steps apply only to complaint cases.
Most customer interaction remains face to face, consistent with the supplied priors.
The access estimate includes any applicable national consultation; it excludes a disputed approval process.
unknowns: Which purchase and stock interfaces are accessible?
Where are complaints recorded today?
What remedies can the supervisor approve?
Is there capacity and customer demand for booked product-help appointments?
research_questions: Can staff retrieve stock, purchases and policy references from one product or receipt identifier?
How much complaint administration disappears when one record drives the handoff?
new_work: Maintain policy links and remedy limits.
Resolve unmatched receipts and stale stock data.
Check complaint routing and overdue follow-up.
Review access permissions and retention.
tasks.statement: Provide customer service by greeting and assisting customers and responding to customer inquiries and complaints.

tasks.short: Monitor service and goods quality, identify problems and guide corrective action.

steps.what: Review sales, returns and service reports for unusual patterns.
Observe customer interactions, queues and goods quality on the floor.
Read complaint messages and customer comments to identify recurring service or product issues.

loop.input: A fixed daily batch of complaint text and customer comments, with unnecessary identifiers removed.
loop.output: Draft service and product themes linked to supporting record identifiers and excerpts.
loop.check: Validate the output schema and source references; the supervisor checks themes before operational use.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair attempt per batch, within a fixed token budget; unresolved records go to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured counts remain deterministic, but varied free text often expresses the same issue in different words.

steps.what: Choose a service correction or product escalation after checking context.
Give staff specific feedback and demonstrate the required service improvement.
Record the action and arrange a follow-up check.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combine point-of-sale records from {OTHER}, returns from the {ERP} and complaints from the {HELPDESK} into a {BI} exception view. A bounded model pass drafts complaint themes with source excerpts, while the {WORKFLOW} tracks approved actions and follow-up. The supervisor observes service, chooses corrections and delivers coaching.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports and complaint narratives are disconnected. Counts alone do not explain recurring issues, and local action notes are hard to follow through.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic reporting handles the numerical work. Bounded text classification can group complaint wording, with source checks and supervisor review.
tasks.still_hard: Complaint volume and return rates can reflect product mix or trading conditions rather than poor service. GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; extending the model to evaluate individual workers would require a separate employment-risk assessment and applicable national consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a service failure from an unfair complaint and coach staff with context, restraint and practical examples.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time assembling evidence and can review recurring issues daily. Coaching and consequential staff decisions remain human; no additional personnel authority is assumed.

reach.task: Select service improvements across departments or stores.
reach.learn: Learn comparable service measures, product-mix effects and how to test whether a correction worked.

evidence.claim: Scheduled operational reports and dashboards can use deterministic processing without a model.
Bounded classification can draft complaint themes, but accuracy and review time need local validation.
Sales-coaching experiments found differing responses by agent group and benefits from manager-mediated feedback; transfer to retail remains unproven.
AI monitoring or evaluation of worker performance is within the cited employment high-risk category.

assumptions: Returns, complaints and sales can be linked at store and product level.
The model groups service and product issues without scoring individual employees.
Complaint reading is more prominent than the supplied weak mail-share prior suggests.
Consultation and access estimates include privacy review and applicable national employee consultation.
unknowns: How much usable complaint text exists?
Do complaints identify employees or contain sensitive customer information?
Which reporting feeds are timely and complete?
Which national consultation arrangements apply?
Who can approve and fund recurring service improvements?
research_questions: Do drafted themes match supervisor labels on a representative complaint sample?
Are structured complaint categories already sufficient to eliminate the model step?
Can service measures distinguish trading conditions from correctable process problems?
new_work: Review draft themes and unsupported classifications.
Maintain issue categories and source-reference checks.
Monitor missing feeds and changes in return coding.
Keep individual employee evaluation outside the theme classifier.
Check whether completed service actions reduced recurrence.
tasks.statement: Monitor sales activities to ensure that customers receive satisfactory service and quality goods.

tasks.short: Allocate daily store duties around available staff, customer demand and practical constraints.

steps.what: Check the shift roster, absences and recorded qualifications in the {HCM}.
Walk the floor and ask staff about queues, deliveries and immediate constraints.
Choose staff assignments and write the duty sheet.
Brief staff on assignments, resolve concerns and explain priority changes.
Update the duty board so staff can see the agreed assignments.

tasks.design: Configure a duty board in the {WORKFLOW}, drawing availability and qualifications from the {HCM}. Deterministic checks flag coverage gaps, break conflicts and qualification mismatches; the supervisor chooses and approves assignments before publication and approves later changes in the same board.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability, floor conditions and informal staff constraints were separated, so supervisors coordinated through conversation and a handwritten board.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms, connectors and constraint checks can replace copying without requiring a model to judge employees.
tasks.still_hard: Fair rotation, last-minute constraints and explaining unpopular assignments require judgement. Working-time limits and consultation depend on national rules; GDPR applies to staff data, and later AI allocation based on behaviour or traits needs EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor balances immediate coverage with fairness, confidence and staff circumstances that should not become permanent scores.

ambition.what: Rebalance floor coverage when an unexpected queue or delivery changes the shift.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into copying assignments and checking availability. The supervisor can make quicker within-shift changes within existing authority; staffing budgets and contractual hours remain separate decisions.

reach.task: Plan coverage for a store promotion.
reach.learn: Translate expected customer demand into coverage requirements and compare them with actual service gaps.

evidence.claim: Quinyx supports demand-based schedules, working-time constraints and staff shift swaps; this supports the availability layer.
The cited Netherlands works-council provisions cover working-time schemes, staff-data arrangements and performance-monitoring tools.
AI allocation based on behaviour or traits and AI performance evaluation are listed employment use cases.
A configured duty board with deterministic checks can support human assignment decisions without autonomous allocation.

assumptions: The shift roster already exists; this task assigns duties within it.
Floor observation and briefings remain substantial, as the supplied priors suggest.
The design uses availability, required qualifications and explicit constraints rather than inferred personality or performance scores.
Consultation and access estimates cover preparation and review effort; elapsed approval time may be longer.
unknowns: Whether the {HCM} exposes timely availability and qualification data.
Whether an existing {WORKFLOW} already supports duty assignments.
The applicable national rules, collective agreements and employee representation arrangements.
Which assignment changes supervisors may approve themselves.
research_questions: Which coverage checks catch useful errors without creating distracting alerts?
Can staff reliably access the duty board during a shift?
new_work: Maintain duty requirements and qualification mappings.
Resolve stale availability and conflicting constraints.
Review whether rotations distribute unpopular duties fairly.
Support staff who cannot access the digital board.
tasks.statement: Assign employees to specific duties.

tasks.short: Direct retail staff across selling, stock counts, cash checks and customer service.

steps.what: Review staffing, sales, stock-count progress and cash exceptions across operational screens.
Walk the floor and ask staff about queues, workload and obstacles.
Choose duty changes and break coverage within working-time and competence constraints.
Brief employees on priorities, duties and safe ways to handle exceptions.
Check completed work and address mistakes or support needs with the employee.
Update the duty sheet and leave unresolved issues for the next supervisor.

tasks.design: A deterministic dashboard combines staffing from the {HCM} and workforce-management system {OTHER} with stock status from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and cash exceptions from the {ERP}. Configure working-time checks in {OTHER} and a shared duty record in the {WORKFLOW}; the supervisor chooses assignments, briefs staff and checks their work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operational status is fragmented, while duty changes live in local documents and verbal handovers. Assignment decisions also depend on facts learned on the floor.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workforce configuration can enforce rule limits. Small integrations can assemble shift status and retain approved changes without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Fair assignments, staff capability and conflict require direct judgement. GDPR applies to staff records, national consultation rules may apply, and adding AI-based allocation or evaluation would require EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Notice overload, balance fairness with urgency and give clear direction without undermining staff confidence.
tasks.altitude: Screen checking and handover administration shrink, while floor supervision remains central. The supervisor can review coverage more consistently; formal assignment and staffing rights do not automatically change.

reach.task: Plan staffing capacity against trading demand.
reach.learn: Learn demand patterns, labour-cost measures and the limits of short-term redeployment.

evidence.claim: Quinyx supports demand-based schedules, working-time constraints and shift swaps; this supports configuration before custom scheduling.
A vendor case reports faster scheduling at Kendra Scott; it does not establish savings for daily floor supervision.
AI allocation based on behaviour or traits, and AI performance monitoring or evaluation, fall within the cited employment high-risk category.
Staff-record access, national consultation requirements and any consequential automated decisions need review before rollout.

assumptions: The dashboard uses operational exceptions rather than employee rankings.
Assignment choices stay with the supervisor.
The estimate includes access work and applicable national employee consultation.
Most observation, direction and support remain human, consistent with the supplied priors.
unknowns: Which workforce-management and operational interfaces are available?
Which working-time agreements and national consultation requirements apply?
Are competence records reliable enough to support duty checks?
Who may change coverage, breaks and overtime?
research_questions: Which existing workforce settings already cover duty and break constraints?
Can aggregate queue and work-status data support coverage reviews without individual monitoring?
new_work: Maintain working-time and competence constraints.
Investigate missing or delayed operational feeds.
Keep the shift handover concise and current.
Review staff access and changes to the monitoring purpose.
tasks.statement: Direct and supervise employees engaged in sales, inventory-taking, reconciling cash receipts, or in performing services for customers.

tasks.short: Count stock, reconcile inventory, and reorder items below agreed levels.

steps.what: Count shelf and backroom stock and identify damaged or misplaced items.
Investigate discrepancies and approve corrections to recorded stock.
Compare available stock and incoming orders with reorder levels.
Adjust quantities for promotions, shelf space, spoilage, and supplier constraints.
Approve and submit the purchase order within delegated spending limits.
Check supplier confirmation and chase changed quantities or delivery dates.

tasks.design: Configure count entry and reorder rules in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, accounting for available stock, incoming orders, pack sizes, and lead times. Feed proposals to the {PROCUREMENT} for supervisor-approved release, then match structured confirmations through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} and route delivery exceptions to the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical discrepancies undermined recorded stock, while order and supplier information lived in separate places.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing inventory controls support threshold replenishment and count entry. Small integrations can account for incoming orders and match structured supplier confirmations without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Physical counting, shrinkage investigations, unreliable lead times, and unusual promotions remain human work. Email-only suppliers may prevent deterministic confirmation matching.
tasks.human_edge: Staff recognise damaged, misplaced, or unsellable stock and judge when local trading conditions justify an override.

ambition.what: Daily review of imminent shelf gaps

tasks.altitude: The supervisor reviews replenishment exceptions and shelf availability instead of recalculating routine quantities. Purchase authority stays within existing spending limits.

reach.task: Resolve supplier order and delivery discrepancies
reach.learn: Interpret pack sizes, acknowledgements, delivery commitments, and duplicate-order controls.

evidence.claim: Retail forecasting and replenishment software supports replacing manual planning across stores.
Threshold replenishment, open-order checks, and pack-size rounding can use deterministic rules.
Physical stock verification remains necessary when recorded stock is unreliable.

assumptions: The supervisor has delegated responsibility for at least some store replenishment.
Physical counting remains substantial, consistent with the task's strong in-person prior.
Supplier confirmations are available in structured form through the {PARTNER_PORTAL} for the initial scope.
The design does not introduce cameras or individual staff monitoring.
unknowns: Are replenishment decisions made locally or by a central buying team?
How accurate are stock balances and open purchase orders?
Which suppliers provide structured confirmations?
Which items need expiry, batch, or minimum-order controls?
research_questions: Can existing {OPS_SYSTEM} configuration cover reorder calculations and mobile count entry?
Which duplicate-order and delivery-date checks can run before submission?
new_work: Maintain reorder thresholds, pack sizes, and lead times.
Investigate recurring stock discrepancies.
Resolve unmatched supplier confirmations.
Review overrides and check whether they improved availability.
tasks.statement: Inventory stock and reorder when inventory drops to a specified level.

tasks.short: Maintain accurate sales, purchasing and requisition records and resolve transaction mismatches.

steps.what: Export daily sales from the point-of-sale {OTHER}.
Retrieve purchase orders and requisitions from the {PROCUREMENT}.
Combine exports into the store transaction register in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Check totals, missing references and duplicates against source records.
Investigate mismatches with colleagues and send correction requests to the finance team.
Approve supported corrections and amend financial records in the {ERP}.
File the reconciled register and correction evidence in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Scheduled connectors load point-of-sale {OTHER} and {PROCUREMENT} records into a controlled transaction register on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, removing the copied workbook. Deterministic checks create exceptions in the {WORKFLOW}; the supervisor investigates, the finance team approves corrections in the {ERP}, and evidence is archived in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate transaction identifiers, export formats and correction responsibilities made a local workbook the practical bridge.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces and deterministic reconciliation are sufficient; AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings and exception screens.
tasks.still_hard: Returns, late postings, partial deliveries and legacy identifiers complicate matching. Corrections need financial controls, while customer-linked records need GDPR access and retention controls.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor explains what happened in the store and distinguishes a data fault from a genuine operational loss.

ambition.what: Resolve transaction discrepancies during the trading week before period-end reconciliation.

tasks.altitude: Routine copying largely disappears and the supervisor works from an exception queue. The supervisor gains earlier visibility into record gaps; financial posting rights remain with the finance team.

reach.task: Resolve an order whose requisition, receipt and transaction references disagree.
reach.learn: Trace identifiers across source records and distinguish timing differences from missing transactions.

evidence.claim: Scheduled transaction ingestion, duplicate checks, total reconciliation and approval routing need no model when source records are structured.
The digest provides no documented deployment of this exact retail transaction-record workflow.

assumptions: Core sales and purchase records already originate in business systems.
A shared workbook bridges systems in the baseline; this is a modelling assumption.
The structured source records justify more screen-based work than the supplied means prior suggests.
The register supports operations and does not replace the statutory ledger.
Build estimates assume supported exports or interfaces and a limited initial store scope.
unknowns: Which system holds requisitions and purchase records.
Whether a duplicate store register is maintained today.
Source identifiers, export availability and historical data quality.
Which corrections require finance approval.
Retention requirements and permitted access to customer-linked transactions.
research_questions: What share of apparent mismatches disappear after an agreed posting delay?
Which source totals and identifiers provide reliable reconciliation controls?
new_work: Monitor failed imports and source schema changes.
Investigate unmatched transactions and maintain matching rules.
Review correction approvals and access logs.
Test recovery and prevent duplicate processing after retries.
tasks.statement: Keep records of purchases, sales, and requisitions.

tasks.short: Enforce safety, health, and security rules through observation, intervention, and follow-up.

steps.what: Check current rules and outstanding hazards in {DOCS}.
Walk the shop floor and stockroom, checking hazards and working practices.
Stop unsafe activity, explain the rule, and make the area safe.
Write an incident or hazard record using the form in {DOCS}.
Email corrective actions, owners, and deadlines to the responsible team.
Inspect the correction and confirm the hazard can be closed.

tasks.design: Configure a hazard register and corrective action flow in the {WORKFLOW}, using approved rules from {DOCS}. Generate shift checklists, route supervisor-approved assignments, and remind owners about overdue actions. The supervisor still observes conditions, intervenes immediately, and verifies closure.
tasks.previous_blocker: Enforcement depends on physical observation and cooperation. Documents and email often separate hazard records from follow-up.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable forms, permissions, reminders, and action registers cover the administrative work without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising emerging danger, challenging unsafe behaviour, and verifying a real correction require presence and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor intervenes at the right moment and explains rules in a way staff can act on.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time assembling checklists and chasing corrective actions. Immediate safety authority and formal escalation rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve recurring safety issues across stores.
reach.learn: How to distinguish a local lapse from a training, equipment, or staffing problem.

evidence.claim: A configured action register can automate reminders while leaving safety intervention and verification with people.
In the Netherlands, works council consent can apply to schemes involving staff data and performance observation.
GDPR applies to identifiable incident records; access and retention should reflect their purpose and sensitivity.

assumptions: The company has approved safety rules and a named escalation route.
The register supports hazard resolution rather than individual performance scoring.
The access range includes applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Operating countries and applicable employee consultation arrangements.
Whether incident records contain health information or allegations about named staff.
Existing incident reporting tools and emergency procedures.
Who can assign corrective actions and authorise reopening an area.
research_questions: Which national safety reporting, consultation, and incident retention rules apply?
new_work: Maintain checklists, escalation routes, and action owners.
Review overdue actions and verify closure evidence.
Manage restricted access and retention for sensitive records.
Resolve duplicate reports and notification failures.
tasks.statement: Enforce safety, health, and security rules.

tasks.short: Inspect incoming goods, decide whether they are acceptable, and record defects.

steps.what: Compare incoming goods with the delivery record in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Examine goods for damage, spoilage, missing parts, and category-specific defects.
Decide which goods to accept, hold, or escalate under acceptance criteria.
Enter inspection findings and disposition in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Email the buying team defect details and supporting photographs.

tasks.design: Configure a receipt checklist in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with delivery references, defect codes, photographs, and disposition fields. Saving a completed inspection sends a defect referral through the {WORKFLOW} to the buying team and supplies a supplier defect view in the {BI}. Physical examination and acceptance decisions remain with the store supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical condition requires direct examination. Recording defects separately from delivery records also made reporting costly.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing receipt forms, mobile capture, and rule-based notifications can connect inspection records with little custom code.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden damage, specialist product checks, and disagreements about supplier responsibility remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor notices unusual defects and judges whether goods meet customer expectations and acceptance criteria.

ambition.what: Monthly supplier defect feedback for the buying team

tasks.altitude: The week contains less receipt lookup and duplicate reporting, while physical inspection remains the main work. No purchasing or supplier settlement rights change.

reach.task: Resolve delivery discrepancies against purchase orders.
reach.learn: Delivery references, discrepancy codes, and evidence needed for a supplier claim.

evidence.claim: Structured receipt records and rule-based notifications can reduce inspection administration without automating physical examination.
The digest provides no documented case of automated physical condition inspection for this task.

assumptions: A typical store uses the {OPS_SYSTEM} for stock receipts and {EMAIL} for exceptions.
The inspection form can be configured without replacing the stock system.
The estimate excludes cameras, computer vision, and specialist testing equipment.
unknowns: Product categories and required inspection methods.
Whether the {OPS_SYSTEM} supports mobile forms, attachments, and receipt-level permissions.
Who may accept, quarantine, or reject goods.
Current inspection volume and time spent entering findings.
research_questions: Which statutory inspection and retention requirements apply to the confirmed product categories?
new_work: Maintain category-specific acceptance criteria and defect codes.
Resolve unmatched delivery references and failed notifications.
Review recurring defects with the buying team.
tasks.statement: Examine products purchased for resale or received for storage to assess the condition of each product or item.

tasks.short: Hire, develop and evaluate retail staff, with human decisions on promotion and dismissal.

steps.what: Define the vacancy and required skills from staffing needs.
Interview shortlisted candidates and record job-related evidence.
Select a candidate and approve proposed employment terms.
Prepare and send the approved employment offer.
Create the employee record after offer acceptance.
Assign required courses and plan supervised shop-floor practice.
Demonstrate selling skills, observe practice and give feedback.
Gather sales results, training completion and documented observations for evaluation.
Discuss performance, hear the employee's account and agree development actions.
Decide whether to recommend promotion, formal support or dismissal.
Check evidence and national procedures, then approve or return the proposed action.
Explain the approved action privately to the employee.

tasks.design: Configure vacancy templates, approved offer generation and starter workflows across the {ATS}, {ESIGN} and {HCM}, with role-based course assignment in the {LMS}. A deterministic evidence pack joins authorised records from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {LMS} and {TALENT}; managers conduct interviews, coaching and employment decisions, while the {WORKFLOW} routes approvals and follow-up records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recruitment, learning and performance records sit in separate systems. Managers bridge them manually, while employment decisions require contextual evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured workflows and inexpensive connectors can reuse approved records and templates. Automated scoring or a model is unnecessary for this scope.
tasks.still_hard: Sales attribution, unequal shift opportunities, incomplete observations and national employment procedures complicate fair evaluation.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, recognise improvement, hear explanations and take responsibility for consequential employment decisions.

ambition.what: A structured first-month coaching programme for new retail staff

tasks.altitude: Less paperwork creates time for observed practice and earlier support conversations. Hiring, promotion and dismissal authority remains with the existing authorised roles.

reach.task: Calibrate development priorities across stores.
reach.learn: Fair comparisons, opportunity differences and evidence-based coaching.

reach.task: Mentor a new starter during supervised selling practice.
reach.learn: Demonstration, specific feedback and checking understanding.

evidence.claim: Approved templates, course assignment and factual evidence assembly can use configured workflows and deterministic integrations.
Experiments with fintech sales agents found manager-relayed AI feedback performed better than either alone; this is not retail-specific evidence.
The Netherlands has works-council consent provisions covering specified employee-data and performance-observation schemes.
The AI Act identifies specified employment evaluation and task-allocation uses as high-risk; introducing those uses requires a separate assessment.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects, subject to its conditions and exceptions.

assumptions: This is a branched personnel lifecycle; hiring, routine reviews and dismissal do not happen in every instance.
Time shares represent the task across a typical mix of cases, including supporting roles.
The design assembles existing evidence without automated candidate ranking, employee scoring or inferred traits.
Consultation and access ranges include possible employee representation review under national rules.
Existing approved templates and retention rules are available.
unknowns: Which hiring and personnel decisions are delegated to the supervisor?
Which national employment rules and collective agreements apply?
What consultation or consent is required for the proposed employee-data use?
Can sales results be attributed fairly to individuals?
Which records may each manager access, and for how long?
Are recruitment shortlisting and personnel record updates handled centrally?
research_questions: What consultation is required under the applicable national rules?
If scope later includes AI evaluation, what classification and obligations apply under current EU law?
Verify the digest's cited AI Act amendment and application dates before relying on its timeline.
new_work: Check evidence packs for attribution errors and missing context.
Maintain role profiles, course mappings and employment templates.
Handle employee corrections and disputed records.
Review access permissions, retention and connector failures.
Coordinate required employee consultation before changing data use.
tasks.statement: Hire, train, and evaluate personnel in sales or marketing establishments, promoting or firing workers when appropriate.

tasks.short: Cover shop-floor work by cleaning, arranging merchandise, advising customers and completing sales.

steps.what: Inspect the floor and choose the most urgent work to cover.
Clean the work area and remove immediate obstructions.
Replenish shelves and arrange merchandise to the display guide.
Understand the customer's needs, demonstrate products and help them choose.
Complete checkout in the point-of-sale {OTHER}.
Write completed work and unresolved gaps on the shift handover sheet.

tasks.design: Configure quick product and stock lookup from the {DOCS} and {OPS_SYSTEM} alongside the existing point-of-sale {OTHER}. A short handover form in the {WORKFLOW} carries unfinished work into the next shift, while cleaning, shelf handling and customer conversations remain hands-on.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most of the task is physical service; software could only improve supporting information and handover.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search, stock views and short forms can reduce lookup and recording effort without new autonomous systems.
tasks.still_hard: Physical work, interruptions and personal service dominate the time. Stock accuracy and usable access on the shop floor limit the benefit.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor spots a hazard, makes a display work in the real space and responds to a customer's uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: The week remains largely hands-on, with slightly less product searching and handover writing. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Give a short product demonstration suited to the customer's intended use.
reach.learn: Select a useful demonstration and check understanding without pressuring the customer.

evidence.claim: Product lookup and structured handovers can assist service, but software alone does not clean or arrange shelves.

assumptions: The design adds no robotics, cameras or employee monitoring.
The existing point-of-sale {OTHER} already supports routine checkout adequately.
Physical and customer-facing work dominates, consistent with the supplied means prior.
Existing devices and stock views can support quick lookup.
unknowns: Whether staff can access product and stock information on the floor.
How accurate stock availability is during trading hours.
Whether a paper handover is used today.
Whether any changed staff-data arrangements require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Does quick lookup reduce interruptions during customer advice?
Can staff complete a useful handover with fewer fields than the current sheet?
new_work: Keep product guides and stock links current.
Resolve stale handover items.
Maintain shared-device access and sign-out arrangements.
tasks.statement: Perform work activities of subordinates, such as cleaning and organizing shelves and displays and selling merchandise.

tasks.short: Set department goals and procedures, secure approval, and put them into practice.

steps.what: Review trading results, incidents, customer feedback, and existing policies.
Discuss practical problems and proposed changes with staff.
Choose department priorities, targets, and proposed operating changes.
Write procedures, responsibilities, measures, and implementation dates.

loop.input: Chosen priorities, approved source policies, consultation notes, and a fixed procedure template.
loop.output: A procedure draft with source references, responsibilities, measures, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields and references; the supervisor checks accuracy and rejects unsupported policy changes.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved conflicts return to the supervisor for manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but converting varied operational notes into clear instructions requires language drafting.

steps.what: Review the procedure and approve changes within management authority.
Publish the approved procedure and assign implementation actions.
Brief staff, demonstrate changed practices, and resolve questions.

tasks.design: Configure an evidence view in the {BI} and a versioned procedure template in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop turns the supervisor's chosen priorities into a draft; after management approval, the {WORKFLOW} publishes it and creates implementation actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy choices depend on context and staff acceptance. Templates existed, but turning decisions into consistent procedures still required writing and follow-up.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded model loop can draft from a small approved source set. Existing document approval and task workflows handle publication and follow-up deterministically.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing fair targets, securing staff support, and resolving conflicts with company policy remain human work. Changes affecting employment arrangements may require consultation under national rules; personal-data use remains subject to GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor judges which changes staff can sustain and explains trade-offs in a way that earns cooperation.

ambition.what: A monthly staff-led procedure improvement trial

tasks.altitude: More time goes to testing operating changes with staff and assessing their effects. The supervisor can propose small trials within existing authority; broader policy and employment decisions retain their current approvers.

reach.task: Translate commercial priorities into department operating goals
reach.learn: Set measurable goals, evaluate small trials, and distinguish local procedures from company policy.

evidence.claim: Templates, bounded drafting, version control, and approval workflows can reduce procedure paperwork.
The digest provides no documented case for automated retail department policy drafting.
Specified working-time, staff-data, and monitoring schemes require works-council consent in the Netherlands.

assumptions: The supervisor proposes local procedures within company policy rather than independently changing employment terms.
The frequent work consists mainly of small operating updates; formal policy changes happen less often.
The drafting loop does not score employees or recommend individual employment decisions.
Consultation effort depends on the substance of the procedure change, not merely the writing tool.
unknowns: Which procedure changes can the supervisor approve independently?
Which source policies are authoritative and current?
Which changes require employee consultation or specialist review?
Where are implementation actions and staff feedback currently recorded?
research_questions: Which template fields and source checks reliably prevent invented obligations?
Can existing {DOCS} approval and versioning features cover publication without custom development?
new_work: Check draft instructions against approved policies and actual store practice.
Maintain templates, source references, and document permissions.
Remove superseded procedures and close implementation actions.
Assess staff feedback and the results of procedure trials.
tasks.statement: Establish and implement policies, goals, objectives, and procedures for the department.

tasks.short: Coach staff through difficult sales and help them practise a suitable response.

steps.what: Hear the salesperson's account and clarify the customer's difficulty.
Find relevant product guidance, returns rules and discount limits in the {DOCS}.
Prepare an example response and identify escalation limits.

loop.input: A short case summary without customer identifiers and approved relevant guidance.
loop.output: A coaching brief with an example response, policy references and escalation limits.
loop.check: Check references and policy limits automatically; the supervisor checks tone and suitability.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing guidance or unresolved conflicts return to the supervisor.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies the structure but cannot adapt wording to an unfamiliar customer situation.

steps.what: Explain the approach, rehearse the conversation and check the salesperson's understanding.
Record agreed actions and any follow-up in the {LMS}.

tasks.design: Configure a policy index in the {DOCS} and a bounded drafting loop that turns a short case summary into a referenced coaching brief. The supervisor approves the brief, coaches the salesperson and records agreed actions through a short form in the {LMS}.

tasks.enabler_now: Existing search and forms handle retrieval and records; bounded text generation can draft examples from approved guidance.

ambition.what: Short practice sessions for unfamiliar customer objections before a salesperson handles them alone.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less policy searching and note writing, with more time for practice. Formal authority over discounts and customer remedies does not change.

reach.task: Handle a difficult customer enquiry within agreed limits.
reach.learn: Practise questioning, de-escalation and recognising when to involve the supervisor.

evidence.claim: Manager-delivered AI coaching outperformed either approach alone in the cited sales-agent experiments; retail transfer remains unproven.
Policy retrieval, structured coaching records and bounded brief drafting are feasible building blocks; the proposed time shares are estimates.

Approved product guidance and sales policies can be indexed.
The target design does not score employees or record conversations.

Whether supervisors have time and a suitable space for practice.

tasks.statement: Instruct staff on how to handle difficult and complicated sales.

tasks.short: Set merchandise pricing policies that meet margin goals and fit local trading conditions.

steps.what: Collect merchandise costs, sales, stock and current prices.
Calculate margins and compare possible price ladders.
Choose margin floors, markdown triggers and local exceptions with the store manager.
Write the policy, worked examples and exception instructions.
Approve the policy within delegated commercial authority.
Enter approved pricing rules and effective dates.

tasks.enabler_now: Existing pricing controls, structured templates and faster integration development make the calculator and release checks affordable. No model breakthrough is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Cost allocation, supplier funding, uncertain demand response and inconsistent price history can distort apparent margins.
tasks.human_edge: Judge customer expectations, competitive positioning and when protecting a relationship outweighs a short-term margin gain.

reach.task: Compare category pricing scenarios against store contribution targets.

tasks.statement: Formulate pricing policies for merchandise, according to profitability requirements.

tasks.short: Estimate demand and choose the product mix and quantities to sell.

steps.what: Retrieve sales, stock, returns, and margin reports from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP}.
Reconcile product codes, periods, and missing data in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss customer requests, upcoming events, and stock gaps with retail salespersons.
Estimate demand and draft product quantities in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Agree product mix and quantities with the buying team within budget and space.
Enter approved quantities into the {OPS_SYSTEM} for replenishment planning.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins {OPS_SYSTEM} and {ERP} records, validates product mappings, and calculates statistical forecasts with stockout and promotion flags. A {BI} view shows forecast ranges, constrained quantity proposals, and recorded supervisor overrides. The {WORKFLOW} captures buying approval before approved quantities are written to the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales history, stock availability, and local knowledge were separated. Maintaining reliable product mappings and forecast checks cost more than building a forecast formula.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forecasting methods, scheduled data jobs, and faster integration development make a small planning service feasible.
tasks.still_hard: Lost sales during stockouts, new products, unusual events, and long supplier lead times limit forecast accuracy.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor recognises local demand changes and balances availability, margin, space, and customer expectations.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling forecasts to reviewing stockout and overstock exceptions. With explicit delegation, the supervisor gains authority to adjust near-term quantities within buying limits; assortment changes still need buying approval.

reach.task: Compare product opportunities and risks across stores.
reach.learn: Forecast bias, stockout effects, margin trade-offs, and the limits of transferring demand between locations.

Statistical forecasting, constraint rules, and scheduled reports can support demand planning without a generative model.

Sales and stock records have usable product and location identifiers.

Rollout starts with a limited product range and historical backtesting.

Supplier lead times, minimum quantities, and delivery constraints.

Monitor failed jobs and duplicate write prevention.
tasks.statement: Estimate consumer demand and determine the types and amounts of goods to be sold.

tasks.short: Inspect merchandise for correct prices, suitable displays and advertised functionality.

steps.what: Read current price changes, display instructions and product checks.
Walk displays and inspect placement, condition, signage and presentation.
Compare shelf labels with scanned prices in the point-of-sale system {OTHER}.
Test selected goods against advertised functions and relevant safety instructions.
Approve corrections, isolate suspect goods or escalate an issue beyond delegated authority.
Record findings and assign approved corrections for completion.

tasks.design: A deterministic checklist combines approved instructions in the {DOCS} with price and promotion records from the point-of-sale system {OTHER}. Configure mobile checks and correction assignments in the {WORKFLOW}; staff still inspect displays, read physical labels and test goods, with approval before corrective action.
tasks.previous_blocker: The decisive evidence is on the shelf or in the product itself. Digital instructions and price records do not show whether a physical display is correct.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured mobile forms and scan lookups can reduce preparation and recording effort. No breakthrough is needed, and the main physical inspection remains.
tasks.still_hard: A correct price record cannot prove that a shelf label matches it. Function checks depend on the product, and unusual safety or advertising claims require specialist escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Spot misleading presentation, physical defects and failures that a records check cannot establish.
tasks.altitude: The week changes only slightly: less checklist preparation and duplicate recording, with physical checks still dominant. No new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Maintain displays and correct shelf-label discrepancies.
reach.learn: Learn promotion effective dates, display standards and when goods must be escalated.

Staff can scan products during inspection.

Build a roster matching coverage, skills, availability, and working-time limits.
Discuss conflicting requests and agree workable shift changes.
Approve the final roster and publish it to staff.
Resolve missing punches and approve actual hours against the roster.
Send approved hours to payroll and retain the scheduling record.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rebuilding rosters to resolving coverage and fairness exceptions. Existing scheduling authority stays with the supervisor; no new employment decision rights are assumed.

tasks.short: Review sales and inventory records and prepare management reports.

steps.what: Retrieve period sales, stock movements, and financial totals.
Reconcile returns, stock adjustments, reporting dates, and missing records.
Calculate sales, margin, stock, and budget variances in the reporting template.
Explain material variances and select issues requiring management attention.
Approve and circulate the report and commentary to management and finance.

tasks.short: Coordinate retail promotions, prepare advertising copy and arrange merchandise displays.

steps.what: Review the campaign brief, stock availability and previous promotion results.
Agree the local offer, audience, budget and display concept with marketing.
Write advertising copy and display instructions using approved campaign materials.

loop.input: Approved product facts, offer terms, channel limits, brand guidance and local campaign plan.
loop.output: Channel copy variants and a draft display instruction sheet.
loop.check: Validate prices, dates and required terms against structured inputs; a person checks claims and clarity.
loop.stop: Generate once and allow one revision; missing facts or failed checks return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard offers; varied local wording and narrative instructions need bounded drafting.

steps.what: Approve claims, offer terms, brand fit and display materials.
Assign setup duties and confirm materials and deadlines with staff.
Schedule approved digital advertisements and posts.
Arrange merchandise, signage and promotional fixtures on the shop floor.
Inspect the display and authorise opening it to customers.
Review campaign sales, stockouts and advertising results.

Approved packs create setup tasks in the {PROJECT} and staged releases in the {ADS} and {SOCIAL}, while the {BI} joins campaign results and store sales.

reach.learn: Audience needs, product claims and practical demonstration planning.

reach.task: Compare promotion contribution across stores.
reach.learn: Baseline selection, stockout effects and the limits of campaign attribution.

Applicable EU discount announcements require prior-price checks; category exceptions and national implementation need validation.

tasks.statement: Plan and coordinate advertising campaigns and sales promotions and prepare merchandise displays and advertising copy.

tasks.short: Work with sales leaders to improve sales, reach customers, and promote the store.

steps.what: Review sales, margin, and promotion results in the {BI}.
Draft sales improvement options and supporting evidence in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved aggregate metrics, local demand notes, previous promotion results, and commercial constraints.
loop.output: A short brief with evidence-linked options, assumptions, and proposed measures of success.
loop.check: Validate metric references and figures against supplied records; the supervisor reviews feasibility and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per brief; unresolved claims are removed or sent for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables can be templated, but connecting free-text local observations to concise proposals needs bounded drafting.

steps.what: Discuss options, local constraints, and customer opportunities with the sales manager.
Approve a pilot, budget, owners, and success criteria.
Email agreed actions and review dates to the delivery team.

After supervisor review and the sales manager's pilot approval, the {WORKFLOW} creates actions in the {PROJECT} and review dates in the {CALENDAR}. Discussions and commercial commitments remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence preparation was fragmented, while useful proposals depended on local context and agreement between teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured reports provide repeatable evidence, and bounded drafting can turn supplied notes into a reviewable brief.
tasks.still_hard: Separating promotion effects from seasonality, winning budget, and coordinating store and marketing capacity remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor brings customer knowledge, tests assumptions in conversation, and builds agreement around practical changes.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time preparing meeting materials and more time proposing and assessing small commercial experiments. Pilot design can become a delegated responsibility; spending and campaign approval remain with the relevant managers.

reach.learn: Commercial case writing, comparison groups, incremental margin, and clear stop-or-continue criteria.

reach.learn: Customer objections, demonstration design, and how to measure interest without collecting unnecessary personal data.

tasks.statement: Confer with company officials to develop methods and procedures to increase sales, expand markets, and promote business.

tasks.short: Propose store credit policies and operating procedures within finance and legal limits.

steps.what: Review overdue balances, credit losses and recurring operational exceptions.
Compare current procedures with central policy and documented exceptions.

loop.input: Versioned central policy, local procedures and documented exception descriptions.
loop.output: Proposed gap list with source passages and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require a source passage for every gap; the supervisor verifies meaning and completeness.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass; conflicting or missing sources go to the policy owner.

steps.what: Approve the policy after required legal review.
Configure approved credit controls and publish the effective procedure.
Brief staff on changed procedures and practise handling exceptions.

tasks.previous_blocker: Policy documents and operational exceptions are disconnected. Translating prose into consistent procedures and controls takes repeated manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned records, configured credit controls and bounded document processing can support the work without autonomous credit decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Credit authority, consumer versus business credit, conflicting procedures and national rules determine what local policy may change.

tasks.short: Plan store budgets and approve payments and merchandise returns within delegated limits.

Decide the return exception and explain the outcome to the customer.
Record the return decision, authorization and stock disposition.
Process the authorized refund or exchange and issue a receipt.
Review budget variances and identify spending requiring intervention.
